agents.name: Duplicate Agent
agents.statement: The same invoice cannot be paid twice.
agents.mechanism: Every arriving invoice is matched against every invoice that vendor has ever sent — the portal, the shared mailbox, the one handed to someone at the site office. The channel is not a hiding place.
agents.lede: Duplicates are not a fraud problem. They are a filing problem that costs real money, and they survive because the second copy usually arrives through a different door than the first.
checks: Invoice number against every prior invoice from the same vendor, not just the current period
Same amount, same date, same PO — the near-match that a changed invoice number is meant to hide
The same document arriving on a second channel after it was already booked
Credit notes that reverse an invoice which was never actually paid
reads: Vendor invoices from every channel — portal, email, file drop, scanned paper
The full invoice history for that vendor
writes: A hold on the second copy, before it can enter a payment run
The matching earlier invoice, attached, so the reviewer can see why
An audit entry recording what matched and who released it
agents.ambiguity: A near-match is not a duplicate. Where the amount and date align but the invoice number does not, the entry is held and both documents are put side by side for a person to decide — it is not silently released, and it is not silently blocked.

agents.name: Pricing Agent
agents.statement: Nothing is paid above the rate that was agreed.
agents.mechanism: Every line is checked against the contract and the PO it belongs to. A variance does not get approved quietly — it stops, and it names the buyer who owns the contract.
agents.lede: This is the largest of the six leaks, and the most ordinary. The contract says one number, the invoice says another, and nobody opens the contract for a bill this size.
checks: Line rate against the contracted rate for that item, that vendor, that period
Rate against the PO, where a PO exists and the contract does not cover the item
Price escalations claimed against the escalation clause that permits them
Freight, handling and surcharges against what the contract actually allows to be added
reads: The vendor contract and its rate schedule
writes: A hold on the line, with the variance in both percentage and rupees
The contract clause the line was tested against
A note to the buyer who owns the contract
agents.ambiguity: Where no contract covers the item, the agent says so rather than passing the line. An uncovered rate is a different finding from an overcharge, and it is reported as its own thing — usually it means a contract expired and nobody renewed it.

agents.name: 3-way match Agent
agents.statement: Nothing is paid for that wasn't received.
agents.mechanism: PO, GRN and invoice have to agree on quantity, rate and item before the entry stands. All three, on every line, every time.
agents.lede: The invoice bills 82 MT. The gate received 78. Both facts are true, and they live in different systems, which is why the difference is usually found in a stock reconciliation months later.
checks: Invoiced quantity against goods actually received, line by line
Item and specification, not just the total — a substituted grade at the contracted rate is still a variance
Partial deliveries billed as complete
Tolerances you define, applied consistently rather than at each approver's discretion
reads: Goods receipt notes from the plant or warehouse system
writes: A short-receipt finding with the quantity gap priced
The GRN reference the invoice was tested against
A hold until the gap is explained or the invoice is revised
agents.ambiguity: Where the GRN has not arrived yet, the invoice is not failed — it is parked as awaiting receipt, with the age of the wait visible. A missing GRN and a short receipt are different problems and are never merged into one.

agents.name: GST Agent
agents.statement: Input credit is never claimed before the vendor has earned it.
agents.mechanism: The vendor's filing status is checked at the point of entry, not discovered at the annual return when the credit has already been taken and spent.
agents.lede: Input credit depends on someone else's compliance. If the vendor has not filed, the credit was never yours to take — and finding that out a year later means reversing it with interest.
checks: Vendor GSTIN active and valid on the invoice date
Filing status for the relevant period before the credit is claimed
Place of supply, and whether the tax charged is the tax that should have been charged
Invoice appearing in the vendor's outward supplies, matched against what was booked
writes: A hold on the credit claim, not on the payment, where the vendor has not filed
The period and status the decision was based on
A follow-up to the vendor to file
agents.ambiguity: Filing status changes. A credit held today may be claimable next month, so the hold is a queue rather than a rejection — the claim is re-tested as status updates, and released when it qualifies.

agents.name: TDS Agent
agents.statement: Tax is deducted at the right section and the right rate — including when a certificate or a threshold changes it.
agents.mechanism: Section, rate, vendor status and year-to-date position are resolved before the entry is posted — not corrected in a return two quarters later, and not paid out of your own pocket as interest.
agents.lede: Under-deducting is the expensive direction. The shortfall is recoverable from the vendor in theory and almost never in practice, so it becomes a cost plus interest.
checks: The correct section for the nature of the payment, not the one used last time
A lower-deduction certificate under section 197, applied within its limit and validity
Higher rates where they apply — no PAN, or an inoperative one
Annual thresholds, including whether this payment is the one that crosses them
Cumulative deduction against the vendor for the year, so the crossing is caught on the day
reads: Vendor master, PAN status and any section 197 certificate on file
Payment nature and the invoice narration
writes: The section and rate applied, with the reason recorded
A correction where the entry was raised at the wrong rate
A flag when this payment crosses a threshold
agents.ambiguity: Where the nature of a payment is genuinely arguable between two sections, the agent applies the higher-deduction reading and flags it for review, rather than choosing the cheaper one and leaving you exposed.

agents.name: Discount Agent
agents.statement: An early-payment discount that was available is never left unclaimed.
agents.mechanism: Discount terms are read off the contract and the invoice, and the payment run is built to hit the date the discount actually requires.
agents.lede: This is the only one of the six that is not a leak so much as an unopened envelope. The money is offered, the terms are on the invoice, and the approval takes twelve days when the discount needed ten.
checks: Discount terms on the invoice against the terms in the contract, where they differ
The date the discount actually expires, counted from the right event
Whether the run is scheduled to land inside that window
The trade-off, where taking the discount conflicts with a payment date set for cash reasons
writes: A recommended payment date that captures the discount
The value of taking it against the value of holding cash
A record when a discount was consciously let go, and why
agents.ambiguity: Cash position beats a discount sometimes, and that is a treasury decision rather than an accounts one. The agent surfaces the number and the deadline; it does not move a payment date on its own.

agents.name: Payments Agent
agents.statement: A payment run contains only entries that passed every check.
agents.mechanism: Eligibility is decided by what cleared at entry, not by what is due. An invoice that is still held cannot be swept into a run because the date arrived.
agents.lede: The run is the last point at which anything is reversible. Everything after it is a recovery conversation.
checks: Every line in the run traces to an entry that cleared its checks
Held items cannot enter the run because their due date passed
Amounts in the run match the approved entry, not the original invoice
Nothing is in the run twice under two references
reads: Approved entries and their check history
writes: The run, with anything ineligible excluded and the reason recorded
A traceable link from each payment back to the invoice and the checks behind it
agents.ambiguity: Where an entry is eligible but something changed since approval — an amount, a bank account, a vendor status — it leaves the run and is named, rather than being paid on the strength of an approval that no longer describes it.

agents.name: MSME Agent
agents.statement: A registered small vendor is paid inside the statutory window — 45 days, or 15 where nothing was agreed in writing.
agents.mechanism: The clock runs from acceptance or deemed acceptance, not from the invoice date, and which window applies depends on whether there is a written agreement. Both are resolved per vendor and turned into a constraint on the payment run.
agents.lede: Section 15 of the MSMED Act sets the window: the date agreed in writing, never beyond 45 days from acceptance — and just 15 days where nothing was agreed in writing. Section 43B(h) then makes a late payment to a registered micro or small enterprise non-deductible until it is actually paid. Two different consequences, one clock, and nobody with the time to track it per vendor.
checks: Udyam registration and enterprise category against the vendor, not against memory
Which window applies — 45 days on a written agreement, 15 days without one
The day the clock actually started: acceptance or deemed acceptance, not the invoice date
Whether written objection was raised inside 15 days, since that changes the computation
Days remaining on every open invoice, and whether the scheduled run lands inside the window
reads: Purchase terms, and whether they are agreed in writing
writes: Days remaining against every open invoice for a registered vendor
The window applied and why, so the computation can be re-read
A scheduling constraint on the run, and a flag where the window cannot be met
agents.ambiguity: Registration status changes, and a vendor can register after invoicing. Where status or the agreed-in-writing question is unclear, the shorter window is applied and the case is named — assuming the longer one is the expensive direction, because the consequence is both interest and a disallowed deduction.

agents.name: PAN Agent
agents.statement: No payment goes to an unverified PAN.
agents.mechanism: Status and linkage are confirmed before the vendor is paid at the standard rate, because an inoperative PAN means deduction at a much higher rate and the shortfall lands on you.
agents.lede: A PAN that has gone inoperative does not announce itself. It shows up as a demand for the difference, plus interest, long after the payment.
checks: PAN present, valid and active against the vendor
PAN linked, so the higher deduction rate does not apply
Name on the PAN against the name on the invoice
New vendors verified before the first payment rather than after
writes: Verified status against the vendor record
A hold where the PAN would force a higher rate
The evidence behind the decision
agents.ambiguity: Where a name is close but not identical — an initial, a suffix, a legal-entity form — the agent does not decide the match. It shows both and asks, because a wrong assumption here is a wrong deduction on every payment that follows.

agents.name: DOA Agent
agents.statement: Nothing is approved by someone who isn't allowed to approve it.
agents.mechanism: The delegation of authority is applied at entry rather than audited afterwards, against limits and tolerances you define, with every override logged against a named user.
agents.lede: The delegation exists. It is a document. Whether it operated on a given invoice is a separate question, usually answered months later by someone testing a sample.
checks: Approver against the limit for that value, that category, that entity
Splitting — two entries just under a limit that together cross it
Maker and checker are actually different people
Overrides recorded against a named user with a reason
reads: The delegation matrix and your defined limits
The approval chain as it happened
writes: A block where the approval exceeds authority
The rule that was applied
An override log entry where someone went past it deliberately
agents.ambiguity: Where a category is ambiguous and two limits could apply, the lower is enforced and the case is named. It is the reversible direction — an unnecessary approval costs a day, an unauthorised one costs the control.

agents.name: Journal Agent
agents.statement: Every entry that reaches the ledger is balanced and carries its support.
agents.mechanism: Balance, account, period and attachment are checked before the entry is written, so the ledger never holds something that has to be found and fixed later.
agents.lede: An unbalanced or unsupported entry is not caught by the ledger. It is caught by a person, during the close, when there is least time to deal with it.
checks: Debits equal credits, at the entry rather than at the batch
Accounts exist, are active, and are the ones the transaction implies
Supporting document attached and readable
Narration that will still mean something in nine months
writes: A balanced entry into your ERP
The support, attached
The check history against the entry
agents.ambiguity: Where the correct account is genuinely arguable, the entry is not guessed into the nearest one. It is held with the candidates and what distinguishes them.

agents.name: Reconciliation Agent
agents.statement: The sub-ledger agrees to the control account every day, not every month.
agents.mechanism: Matching runs continuously, so a break is found on the day it appears rather than at the close, when its cause is a month cold.
agents.lede: A break found on the day it happened usually has an obvious cause. The same break found five weeks later is an investigation.
checks: Sub-ledger balance against the control account, daily
Bank lines against booked payments
Unmatched items, with an age against each
Breaks that are growing rather than static
writes: The break, with its age and probable cause
Matched items cleared automatically
The reconciliation trail
agents.ambiguity: A probable match is not a match. Where confidence is short of certain, the item stays open with both candidates shown — a wrongly cleared break is worse than an open one, because it stops being visible.

agents.name: Intercompany Agent
agents.statement: Both sides agree before either is posted.
agents.mechanism: The counterparty entity confirms the entry before it lands, so eliminations at consolidation are arithmetic rather than negotiation.
agents.lede: Intercompany differences are not usually errors. They are two entities booking the same transaction on different days, at different amounts, in different currencies, and both being right.
checks: Counterparty entity, amount and date agreed on both sides
Currency and the rate applied on each side
The entry exists in both books before consolidation
Balances that will eliminate cleanly
writes: The agreed entry in both books
A hold where the sides do not agree, showing the difference
The agreement trail
agents.ambiguity: Where the two sides disagree, neither is assumed right. The difference is quantified and put to both entity controllers, because the resolution is a decision about the transaction, not about the bookkeeping.

agents.name: Period Agent
agents.statement: Nothing is posted into a closed period.
agents.mechanism: The period is checked at the moment of posting, and cut-off is applied by the date of the event rather than the date someone got to the paperwork.
agents.lede: Most cut-off errors are not deliberate. They are an invoice for March processed in April, booked on the day it was keyed.
checks: The period is open for this entry type and entity
The event date, not the entry date, decides the period
Accruals raised for what belongs in the period but has not arrived
Prior-period items routed as adjustments rather than posted quietly
writes: The entry in the correct period
An accrual where the document has not arrived
A routed adjustment where the period is closed
agents.ambiguity: Where the event date is genuinely unclear — a service spanning a period end — the entry is split or flagged rather than assigned to whichever period is convenient.

agents.name: Audit Agent
agents.statement: Every decision can be re-read later: what was checked, what was found, who released it.
agents.mechanism: The trail is written as the checks run, immutably, so evidence is a record rather than a reconstruction.
agents.lede: The difference between a control that operated and one that is asserted to have operated is whether anyone can show it, months later, without rebuilding the story.
checks: Every check that ran against the transaction, and its result
Who approved, who overrode, and the reason given
The document version the decision was made on
That the trail cannot be edited after the fact
writes: An immutable record per transaction
Evidence packs that can be handed to an auditor as they are
Control adherence per step
agents.ambiguity: Nothing is omitted for being inconvenient. A check that failed and was overridden is recorded exactly as that, including who decided and why — a trail that only holds the clean cases is not a trail.

agents.name: Report Agent
agents.statement: The books are reportable the day the period ends, without a cleanup pass.
agents.mechanism: Because entries arrived clean, closing is a confirmation rather than a correction exercise.
agents.lede: A close is long in proportion to how much was deferred into it. Nothing is deferred here, so there is nothing waiting.
checks: All entries for the period posted, balanced and supported
Reconciliations complete and breaks explained
Intercompany eliminated
Nothing sitting in a suspense account
reads: The full ledger for the period
writes: Close status, by entity and by step
What remains, with an owner against each
Reports ready without adjustment
agents.ambiguity: The close is not declared complete because a date arrived. Anything unresolved is named and owned, and the status says so rather than rounding to done.

agents.name: Bank Agent
agents.statement: A beneficiary account cannot change silently between approval and payment.
agents.mechanism: Bank details are verified against what was approved, not against what is current in the vendor master — which is the exact gap a vendor-impersonation attempt is built to exploit.
agents.lede: The most expensive fraud in accounts payable is not a fake invoice. It is a real invoice, from a real vendor, paid into an account that changed last week.
checks: Beneficiary account against the one on the approved entry
Any change to vendor bank details since approval, and who made it
Account name against the vendor name
First payments to a newly changed account, held for confirmation
reads: The approved entry and its bank details
writes: A hold where details changed after approval
The change, with who made it and when
Confirmation before the first payment on new details
agents.ambiguity: A legitimate bank change looks identical to a fraudulent one at the moment it is made. So the agent never decides which it is — it stops the first payment on changed details and asks for confirmation through a channel that is not the one the change arrived on.
